newsitem.title: CANADA: Intrawest sees EPS, cash flow increase.
newsitem.headline: Intrawest sees EPS, cash flow increase.

text.p: VANCOUVER, Dec 18 - Intrawest Corp said Tuesday it expects an immediate rise in earnings and cash flow per share as a result of its C$260 million deal to acquire the Whistler Mountain and Copper Mountain ski resorts.
"There will be an immediate positive impact on EPS and cash flow per share," Intrawest chief financial officer Dan Jarvis told reporters.
He declined to project the size of the increase. Intrawest earned C$0.82 a share and had cash flow of C$1.34 a share in its fiscal year ended June 30.
Jarvis said there would be no increase in Intrawest's debt-equity ratio which stood at 1.31 to 1 at the end of its 1996 fiscal year.
Shares issued in the deal to the two families that own Whistler in British Columbia and the one family that owns Copper in Colorado will mean a 20 percent increase in shares outstanding.
The deal involves the assumption of about C$140 million in debt, Jarvis said.

Intrawest president Joe Houssian said the company was still interested in pursuing acquisitions within its focus as a resort developer, possibly of summer-oriented, beach or desert resorts focused on golf.

Intrawest's non-resort assets will be disposed of over two to four years with proceeds being paid to shareholders of a special class of shares as properties are sold. These assets have a book value currently of about C$86 million, Jarvis said.
About a third of that is financial receivables and the rest includes a scattering of properties in British Columbia, Washington state and Alberta.
